hello-polite.meaningNote: Polite morning or afternoon greeting; "po" shows respect toward elders or strangers.

good-morning.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, kumusta po kayo?

good-evening.meaningNote: Greeting used after sunset or once evening falls.
good-evening.exampleSentence: Magandang gabi po, may bakanteng mesa pa po ba?

how-are-you.meaningNote: Derived from Spanish "¿Cómo está?". "Kayo" is the plural or polite singular pronoun.

nice-to-meet-you.meaningNote: Traditional, highly respectful expression when meeting someone new.
nice-to-meet-you.exampleSentence: Ikinagagalak ko po kayong makilala, Ginoong Ramos.

thank-you-very-much.meaningNote: Standard warm expression of gratitude in Filipino culture.
thank-you-very-much.exampleSentence: Maraming salamat po sa inyong tulong.

you-are-welcome.meaningNote: Reply to thanks meaning "it is nothing / do not mention it".
you-are-welcome.exampleSentence: Walang anuman po, masaya akong nakatulong sa inyo.

please.meaningNote: The polite prefix "paki-" (such as "pakikuha" or "pakidala") is also frequently used for requests.
please.exampleSentence: Pakiusap po, pakisuyo naman po ng baso.

excuse-me-pardon.meaningNote: Use "Makikiraan po" when asking to pass through; use "paumanhin" when apologizing.
excuse-me-pardon.exampleSentence: Makikiraan po sandali, kailangan ko lang lumabas.

goodbye-take-care.meaningNote: Polite farewell wishing the other person safety.
goodbye-take-care.exampleSentence: Paalam po, mag-iingat kayo sa inyong biyahe.

a-table-for-two-please.meaningNote: Polite request to a host or server when entering a restaurant.
a-table-for-two-please.exampleSentence: Magandang gabi po, mesa po para sa dalawa sa may bintana.

can-i-see-the-menu.text: Puwede po bang makahingi ng menu?
can-i-see-the-menu.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mah-kah-HEENG-ee nahng MEH-nyoo
can-i-see-the-menu.meaningNote: Polite request for the list of available dishes.
can-i-see-the-menu.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang makahingi ng menu at listahan ng inumin?

what-do-you-recommend.text: Ano po ang specialty o masarap dito?
what-do-you-recommend.pronunciation: ah-NOH poh ahng SPEH-shahl-tee oh mah-sah-RAHP DEE-toh
what-do-you-recommend.meaningNote: Asking about the restaurant's specialty or best-selling dish.
what-do-you-recommend.exampleSentence: Bago lang po kami rito, ano po ang pinakamasarap na ulam dito?

the-check-please.text: Puwede na po bang makuha ang bill?
the-check-please.pronunciation: pweh-DEH nah poh bahng mah-KOO-hah ahng beel
the-check-please.meaningNote: In casual restaurants across the Philippines, saying "Bill out po" is also very common.
the-check-please.exampleSentence: Tapos na po kaming kumain, puwede na po bang makuha ang bill?

i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.text: May allergy po ako sa mani
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.pronunciation: my AH-lehr-jee poh ah-KOH sah mah-NEE
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.meaningNote: Important to tell the server immediately before your food is prepared.
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.exampleSentence: Pakisabihan po ang kusina na may allergy po ako sa mani.

is-this-dish-spicy.text: Maanghang po ba ang pagkaing ito?
is-this-dish-spicy.pronunciation: mah-ahng-HAHNG poh bah ahng pahg-kah-EENG ee-TOH
is-this-dish-spicy.meaningNote: Asking whether the dish contains bird's eye chili (siling labuyo) or spicy ingredients.
is-this-dish-spicy.exampleSentence: Hindi po ako sanay sa sili, maanghang po ba ito?

water-without-ice-please.meaningNote: Request for room-temperature or unchilled water.
water-without-ice-please.exampleSentence: Medyo masama ang lalamunan ko, tubig na lang po na walang yelo.

delicious-compliment.meaningNote: Heartfelt compliment for the cook and kitchen staff.
delicious-compliment.exampleSentence: Napakasarap po ng pagkain, tiyak na babalik kami rito.

is-this-vegetarian.text: Wala po ba itong karne o isda?
is-this-vegetarian.pronunciation: wah-LAH poh bah ee-TOHNG kahr-NEH oh ees-DAH
is-this-vegetarian.meaningNote: Explicitly saying "no meat or fish" is clearer in the Philippines than simply saying "vegetarian".
is-this-vegetarian.exampleSentence: Gulay lang po ang kinakain ko, wala po ba itong halong karne?

can-i-have-this-to-go.meaningNote: Both "ipabalot" (have it wrapped) and "take-out" are commonly understood in the Philippines.
can-i-have-this-to-go.exampleSentence: Medyo marami pa pong natira, puwede po bang ipabalot ito?

what-is-your-name.meaningNote: Polite question using "po" and plural/respectful "ninyo". Casual form is "Anong pangalan mo?".
what-is-your-name.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, ano po ang pangalan ninyo?

it-is-my-first-time-here.text: Unang beses ko pong bumisita rito.
it-is-my-first-time-here.pronunciation: OO-nahng BEH-sehs koh pohng boo-mee-SEE-tah REE-toh
it-is-my-first-time-here.meaningNote: "Beses" (from Spanish "veces") is the standard everyday word for "times" or "occasions".
it-is-my-first-time-here.exampleSentence: Unang beses ko pong bumisita rito sa inyong probinsya.

where-are-you-from.meaningNote: The prefix "taga-" asks which town, province, or country someone comes from.
where-are-you-from.exampleSentence: Masaya pong makilala kayo, taga-saan po kayo?

is-this-your-hometown.meaningNote: Literally asks "Did you grow up here?", which is the most natural way to ask if a place is someone's hometown.
is-this-your-hometown.exampleSentence: Ang ganda po ng bayan ninyo, dito po ba kayo lumaki?

what-do-you-do-for-a-living.meaningNote: "Trabaho" means job or work. A softer, indirect alternative is "Ano po ang pinagkakaabalahan ninyo?" (What keeps you busy?).
what-do-you-do-for-a-living.exampleSentence: Guro po ako sa amin, ano po ang trabaho ninyo rito?

how-long-have-you-lived-here.text: Gaano na po kayo katagal nakatira rito?
how-long-have-you-lived-here.pronunciation: gah-AH-noh nah poh kah-YOH kah-tah-GAHL nah-kah-tee-RAH REE-toh
how-long-have-you-lived-here.meaningNote: Polite way to ask how long someone has resided in a place.
how-long-have-you-lived-here.exampleSentence: Tahimik po sa lugar na ito, gaano na po kayo katagal nakatira rito?

what-do-you-like-to-do.text: Ano po ang hilig ninyong gawin sa libreng oras?
what-do-you-like-to-do.pronunciation: ah-NOH poh ahng HEE-leeg neen-YOHNG gah-WEEN sah LEE-brehng OH-rahs
what-do-you-like-to-do.meaningNote: "Hilig" means hobby or interest, and "sa libreng oras" means during free time.
what-do-you-like-to-do.exampleSentence: Ano po ang hilig ninyong gawin sa libreng oras kapag walang pasok?

that-is-interesting.meaningNote: Literally "How nice/interesting to know that!". In casual conversation, "Ang galing naman!" is also common.
that-is-interesting.exampleSentence: Nakakatuwa naman pong malaman iyan tungkol sa kultura ninyo!

it-was-nice-talking-to-you.meaningNote: Warm, respectful way to close a friendly conversation.
it-was-nice-talking-to-you.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko na pong umalis, masaya po akong nakausap kayo.

have-a-nice-day.text: Magandang araw po sa inyo at ingat po!
have-a-nice-day.pronunciation: mah-gahn-DAHNG AH-raw poh sah een-YOH aht EENG-aht poh
have-a-nice-day.meaningNote: Filipinos frequently wish someone well on parting with "Ingat po!" (Take care) or "Magandang araw po!".
have-a-nice-day.exampleSentence: Maraming salamat po sa kuwentuhan, magandang araw po sa inyo!

how-much-is-this.meaningNote: Standard polite question for asking the price of any item in a shop or market.
how-much-is-this.exampleSentence: Ale, magkano po ito kapag dalawa ang bibilhin?

is-this-available-in-another-size.text: May iba pa po bang size nito?
is-this-available-in-another-size.pronunciation: my ee-BAH pah poh bahng syz nee-TOH
is-this-available-in-another-size.meaningNote: The English loanword "size" (or native "sukat") is universally used in Philippine shops.
is-this-available-in-another-size.exampleSentence: Medyo masikip po ito, may iba pa po bang size nito?

do-you-have-another-color.text: May iba pa po bang kulay nito?
do-you-have-another-color.pronunciation: my ee-BAH pah poh bahng KOO-lye nee-TOH
do-you-have-another-color.meaningNote: "Kulay" is the everyday Filipino word for color.
do-you-have-another-color.exampleSentence: Maganda po ang tela, may iba pa po bang kulay nito?

can-i-try-this-on.text: Puwede ko po bang isukat ito?
can-i-try-this-on.pronunciation: pweh-DEH koh poh bahng ee-SOO-kaht ee-TOH
can-i-try-this-on.meaningNote: "Isukat" means to try on clothes or shoes to check the fit.
can-i-try-this-on.exampleSentence: Puwede ko po bang isukat ito sa fitting room?

is-there-a-discount.meaningNote: The loanword "discount" (or native "bawas") is standard across both malls and markets.
is-there-a-discount.exampleSentence: May discount po ba ito kapag dalawa ang kinuha ko?

can-you-lower-the-price.meaningNote: "Tumawad" is the natural Filipino verb for asking for a friendly price reduction at a market ("palengke" or "tiangge").
can-you-lower-the-price.exampleSentence: Bibili po ako ng tatlo, puwede po bang tumawad nang kaunti?

i-am-just-looking-thank-you.meaningNote: Reduplicating "tingin" ("tumitingin-tingin") softens the verb to mean casually browsing.
i-am-just-looking-thank-you.exampleSentence: Tumitingin-tingin lang po muna ako, tatawagin ko na lang po kayo.

where-can-i-find-this-item.text: Saan ko po makikita ang gamit na ito?
where-can-i-find-this-item.pronunciation: sah-AHN koh poh mah-kee-KEE-tah ahng GAH-meet nah ee-TOH
where-can-i-find-this-item.meaningNote: You can also say "Saan pong banda ito?" (Which section is this in?) when showing an item on your phone.
where-can-i-find-this-item.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, saan ko po makikita ang gamit na ito rito sa tindahan?

can-i-return-this.text: Puwede ko po bang ibalik o ipapalit ito?
can-i-return-this.pronunciation: pweh-DEH koh poh bahng ee-bah-LEEK oh ee-pah-pah-LEET ee-TOH
can-i-return-this.meaningNote: "Ibalik" means to return; "ipapalit" means to exchange. Keep the receipt ("resibo").
can-i-return-this.exampleSentence: Kapag hindi po kasya, puwede ko po bang ibalik o ipapalit ito?

can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.text: Puwede po bang makahingi ng supot?
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mah-kah-HEENG-ee nahng SOO-poht
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.meaningNote: "Supot" is the everyday word for a bag or pouch; in malls and supermarkets, Filipinos also commonly ask for a "paper bag", "plastic bag", or "eco-bag".
can-i-get-a-shopping-bag.exampleSentence: Medyo marami po ito, puwede po bang makahingi ng supot?

what-time-is-it.meaningNote: Filipinos commonly tell time using Spanish-derived numbers (e.g., "alas tres") or English numbers.
what-time-is-it.exampleSentence: Mawalang-galang na po, anong oras na po ngayon?

what-day-is-today.meaningNote: Asks for the day of the week (Lunes, Martes, Miyerkules, etc.).
what-day-is-today.exampleSentence: Anong araw po ngayon, Martes na po ba?

what-is-todays-date.meaningNote: "Petsa" (from Spanish "fecha") refers specifically to the calendar date.
what-is-todays-date.exampleSentence: Magsusulat po ako sa form, anong petsa na po ngayon?

when-does-it-open.meaningNote: When asking store staff directly, you can also say "Anong oras po kayo nagbubukas?".
when-does-it-open.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, anong oras po ito nagbubukas tuwing Linggo?

when-does-it-close.meaningNote: "Nagsasara" means closes; when addressing staff directly, say "Anong oras po kayo nagsasara?".
when-does-it-close.exampleSentence: Hahabol pa po sana kami, anong oras po ito nagsasara mamaya?

how-long-will-it-take.meaningNote: You can also ask "Ilang minuto o oras po ang biyahe?" (How many minutes or hours is the trip?).
how-long-will-it-take.exampleSentence: Kung sasakay po kami ngayon, gaano po ito katagal aabutin?

can-we-meet-tomorrow.text: Puwede po ba tayong magkita bukas?
can-we-meet-tomorrow.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bah TAH-yohng mahg-KEE-tah BOO-kahs
can-we-meet-tomorrow.meaningNote: Uses inclusive "tayo" (we, including the person addressed) and "bukas" (tomorrow).
can-we-meet-tomorrow.exampleSentence: Puwede po ba tayong magkita bukas nang alas diyes ng umaga?

what-time-should-i-come-back.text: Anong oras po ako dapat bumalik?
what-time-should-i-come-back.pronunciation: ah-NOHNG OH-rahs poh ah-KOH DAH-paht boo-mah-LEEK
what-time-should-i-come-back.meaningNote: "Bumalik" means to return or come back.
what-time-should-i-come-back.exampleSentence: Iiwan ko na po muna ito, anong oras po ako dapat bumalik?

two-tickets-please.meaningNote: "Dalawa" (two) takes the linker "-ng" before a noun ("dalawang tiket"). For one, say "isang tiket po"; for three, "tatlong tiket po".
two-tickets-please.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, dalawang tiket po para sa museo.

for-how-many-people.meaningNote: "Ilan" (with linker "ilang") asks "how many". Reply with "Para sa dalawa po" (for two) or "Tatlo po kami" (there are three of us).
for-how-many-people.exampleSentence: Magpapa-reserve po sana kami; para sa ilang tao po ang mesa?

do-you-speak-english.text: Nakakapagsalita po ba kayo ng Ingles?
do-you-speak-english.pronunciation: nah-kah-kah-pahg-sah-lee-TAH poh bah kah-YOH nahng eeng-GLEHS
do-you-speak-english.meaningNote: In the Philippines, English is widely understood, and you can also casually ask "Marunong po ba kayong mag-English?".
do-you-speak-english.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, nakakapagsalita po ba kayo ng Ingles?

i-do-not-understand.text: Pasensya na po, hindi ko po maintindihan.
i-do-not-understand.pronunciation: pah-SEHN-syah nah poh, heen-DEE koh poh mah-een-teen-dee-HAHN
i-do-not-understand.meaningNote: "Pasensya na po" is the most natural everyday way to say "I'm sorry / excuse me" when you do not understand.
i-do-not-understand.exampleSentence: Pasensya na po, hindi ko po maintindihan ang sinabi ninyo.

could-you-speak-more-slowly.text: Puwede po bang pakibagalan nang kaunti ang pagsasalita?
could-you-speak-more-slowly.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng pah-kee-bah-gah-LAHN nahng kah-oon-TEE ahng pahg-sah-sah-lee-TAH
could-you-speak-more-slowly.meaningNote: A shorter everyday alternative is "Pakidahan-dahan lang po sa pagsasalita".
could-you-speak-more-slowly.exampleSentence: Medyo mabilis po, puwede po bang pakibagalan nang kaunti ang pagsasalita?

could-you-repeat-that.meaningNote: "Pakiulit po" is a polite, concise way to say "Please repeat that".
could-you-repeat-that.exampleSentence: Hindi ko po narinig nang malinaw, puwede po bang pakiulit iyon?

could-you-write-it-down.exampleSentence: Baka po makalimutan ko ang pangalan ng kalye, puwede po bang pakisulat dito?

how-do-you-say-this.text: Paano po sabihin ito sa Filipino?
how-do-you-say-this.pronunciation: pah-AH-noh poh sah-BEE-heen ee-TOH sah fee-lee-PEE-noh
how-do-you-say-this.meaningNote: Locals also frequently say "Ano po sa Tagalog ito?" (What is this in Tagalog?).
how-do-you-say-this.exampleSentence: Nag-aaral po ako, paano po sabihin ito sa Filipino?

what-does-this-mean.text: Ano po ang ibig sabihin ng salitang ito?
what-does-this-mean.pronunciation: ah-NOH poh ahng EE-beeg sah-BEE-heen nahng sah-lee-TAHNG ee-TOH
what-does-this-mean.meaningNote: "Ibig sabihin" means meaning, and "salita" means word.
what-does-this-mean.exampleSentence: Ano po ang ibig sabihin ng salitang ito sa karatula?

i-am-learning-your-language.text: Nag-aaral pa lang po akong mag-Filipino.
i-am-learning-your-language.pronunciation: nahg-ah-AH-rahl pah lahng poh ah-KOHNG mahg-fee-lee-PEE-noh
i-am-learning-your-language.meaningNote: "Pa lang" adds the humble nuance "still / just beginning to learn". Locals also say "mag-Tagalog".
i-am-learning-your-language.exampleSentence: Pasensya na po kung mabagal, nag-aaral pa lang po akong mag-Filipino.

please-wait-a-moment.meaningNote: "Sandali lang po" (or "Teka lang po" in casual speech) is the universal way to say "Just a moment, please".
please-wait-a-moment.exampleSentence: Sandali lang po, titingnan ko lang po sa telepono ko.

can-you-show-me.text: Puwede po bang pakipakita sa akin?
can-you-show-me.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng pah-kee-pah-KEE-tah sah AH-keen
can-you-show-me.meaningNote: You can also ask "Puwede po bang paturo?" (Could you show/teach me how?).
can-you-show-me.exampleSentence: Hindi ko po alam gamitin ito, puwede po bang pakipakita sa akin?

this-is-my-family.meaningNote: Used both when introducing your family in person and when showing a family photo.
this-is-my-family.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, ito po ang aking pamilya.

i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.text: Kasama ko po sa biyahe ang mga magulang ko.
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.pronunciation: kah-SAH-mah koh poh sah BYAH-heh ahng mah-NGAH mah-GOO-lahng koh
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.meaningNote: "Biyahe" (trip/travel) is much more natural in everyday conversation than the formal literary verb "naglalakbay".
i-am-traveling-with-my-parents.exampleSentence: Kasama ko po sa biyahe ang mga magulang ko ngayong bakasyon.

do-you-have-children.text: May mga anak na po ba kayo?
do-you-have-children.pronunciation: my mah-NGAH ah-NAHK nah poh bah kah-YOH
do-you-have-children.meaningNote: "Anak" means child (son or daughter), and "mga" makes it plural.
do-you-have-children.exampleSentence: Ang babait po ng mga bata rito, may mga anak na po ba kayo?

where-is-your-family.meaningNote: "Nasaan" asks where a person or thing is located.
where-is-your-family.exampleSentence: Nasaan po ang pamilya ninyo, dito rin po ba sila nakatira?

i-am-here-with-a-friend.text: Kasama ko po rito ang isang kaibigan ko.
i-am-here-with-a-friend.pronunciation: kah-SAH-mah koh poh REE-toh ahng ee-SAHNG kah-ee-BEE-gahn koh
i-am-here-with-a-friend.exampleSentence: Hindi po ako mag-isa, kasama ko po rito ang isang kaibigan ko.

this-is-my-friend.meaningNote: In polite Filipino introductions, "Ito po si..." or "Ipinapakilala ko po ang kaibigan ko" is also used.
this-is-my-friend.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, ito po ang kaibigan ko na si Marco.

this-is-my-partner.meaningNote: Filipinos commonly use the English loanword "partner" in everyday conversation; for a married spouse use "asawa" (gender-neutral), and for a boyfriend/girlfriend "kasintahan" is the formal Tagalog term.
this-is-my-partner.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, ito po ang partner ko na si Sam.

i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.text: May isa po akong kapatid na lalaki at isang kapatid na babae.
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.pronunciation: my ee-SAH poh ah-KOHNG kah-pah-TEED nah lah-LAH-kee aht ee-SAHNG kah-pah-TEED nah bah-BAH-eh
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.meaningNote: "Kapatid" means sibling (gender-neutral); add "na lalaki" for brother or "na babae" for sister, or use "kuya" (older brother) and "ate" (older sister).
i-have-a-brother-and-a-sister.exampleSentence: Tatlo po kaming magkakapatid: may isa po akong kapatid na lalaki at isang kapatid na babae.

do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.text: May mga kapatid po ba kayo?
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.pronunciation: my mah-NGAH kah-pah-TEED poh bah kah-YOH
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.meaningNote: Since "kapatid" means sibling regardless of gender, "mga kapatid" covers both brothers and sisters.
do-you-have-brothers-or-sisters.exampleSentence: May mga kapatid po ba kayo, o nag-iisang anak lang po kayo?

how-old-are-your-children.text: Ilang taon na po ang mga anak ninyo?
how-old-are-your-children.pronunciation: ee-LAHNG tah-OHN nah poh ahng mah-NGAH ah-NAHK neen-YOH
how-old-are-your-children.meaningNote: "Ilang taon" literally means "how many years old".
how-old-are-your-children.exampleSentence: Ang lalaki na po nila, ilang taon na po ang mga anak ninyo?

where-is-the-bathroom.meaningNote: Restrooms are commonly called "banyo" or "CR" (Comfort Room) in the Philippines.
where-is-the-bathroom.exampleSentence: Mawalang-galang na po, saan po ang banyo rito?

how-do-i-get-to-the-station.text: Paano po pumunta sa istasyon ng tren?
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.pronunciation: pah-AH-noh poh poo-moon-TAH sah ees-tahs-YOHN nahng trehn
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.meaningNote: Asking for directions to a train station (such as the LRT, MRT, or commuter rail).
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.exampleSentence: Naliligaw po ako, paano po pumunta sa istasyon ng tren?

is-it-far-from-here.meaningNote: Checking whether a destination is walkable or requires taking a ride.
is-it-far-from-here.exampleSentence: Malayo po ba mula rito ang pamilihan kung lalakarin?

turn-left-at-the-corner.text: Kumaliwa po kayo pagdating sa kanto
turn-left-at-the-corner.pronunciation: koo-mah-lee-WAH poh kah-YOH pahg-dah-TEENG sah KAHN-toh
turn-left-at-the-corner.meaningNote: "Kumaliwa" is the verb for turning left.
turn-left-at-the-corner.exampleSentence: Kumaliwa po kayo pagdating sa kanto sa tapat ng botika.

turn-right-after-the-bank.text: Kumanan po kayo paglampas ng bangko
turn-right-after-the-bank.pronunciation: koo-MAH-nahn poh kah-YOH pahg-lahm-PAHS nahng BAHNG-koh
turn-right-after-the-bank.meaningNote: "Kumanan" is the verb for turning right using a landmark.
turn-right-after-the-bank.exampleSentence: Kumanan po kayo paglampas ng malaking bangko sa kanto.

go-straight-ahead.meaningNote: Continue walking in the same direction without turning.
go-straight-ahead.exampleSentence: Dire-diretso lang po kayo hanggang makita ninyo ang arko.

where-am-i-on-the-map.text: Nasaan po ako rito sa mapa?
where-am-i-on-the-map.pronunciation: nah-SAH-ahn poh ah-KOH REE-toh sah MAH-pah
where-am-i-on-the-map.meaningNote: Asking someone to point out your current location on a map.
where-am-i-on-the-map.exampleSentence: Medyo nalilito po ako, nasaan po ako rito sa mapa?

is-it-within-walking-distance.text: Kaya po bang lakarin mula rito?
is-it-within-walking-distance.pronunciation: KAH-yah poh bahng lah-kah-REEN MOO-lah REE-toh
is-it-within-walking-distance.meaningNote: Checking if the distance is short enough that you do not need public transit.
is-it-within-walking-distance.exampleSentence: Kaya po bang lakarin mula rito papunta sa museo?

where-is-the-bus-stop.text: Saan po ang sakayan ng bus o dyip?
where-is-the-bus-stop.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng sah-kah-YAHN nahng boos oh jeep
where-is-the-bus-stop.meaningNote: In the Philippines, travelers commonly ask for the bus or jeepney stop ("sakayan").
where-is-the-bus-stop.exampleSentence: Saan po ang sakayan ng bus papuntang kabayanan?

i-am-lost-can-you-help.text: Naliligaw po ako, puwede po bang magpatulong?
i-am-lost-can-you-help.pronunciation: nah-lee-lee-GOW poh ah-KOH, pweh-DEH poh bahng mahg-pah-TOO-lohng
i-am-lost-can-you-help.meaningNote: Polite request for help when you have lost your way.
i-am-lost-can-you-help.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, naliligaw po ako, puwede po bang magpatulong?

where-is-baggage-claim.text: Saan po ang kuhanin ng bagahe?
where-is-baggage-claim.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng koo-HAH-neen nahng bah-GAH-heh
where-is-baggage-claim.meaningNote: Area where checked luggage is picked up at an airport or seaport.
where-is-baggage-claim.exampleSentence: Kakarating lang po namin, saan po ang kuhanin ng bagahe?

i-have-a-hotel-reservation.text: May reservation po ako sa pangalang ito
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.pronunciation: my reh-sehr-bahs-YOHN poh ah-KOH sah pah-NGAH-lahng ee-TOH
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.meaningNote: Spoken to the hotel front desk receptionist at check-in.
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, may reservation po ako sa pangalang Juan Cruz.

what-time-is-checkout.text: Anong oras po ang check-out bukas?
what-time-is-checkout.pronunciation: ah-NOHNG OH-rahs poh ahng chehk-owt BOO-kahs
what-time-is-checkout.meaningNote: Confirming the time by which you need to vacate your room.
what-time-is-checkout.exampleSentence: Anong oras po ang check-out bukas para maihanda ang gamit?

how-much-is-a-ticket-to.text: Magkano po ang pamasahe papuntang sentro?
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.pronunciation: mahg-KAH-noh poh ahng pah-mah-SAH-heh pah-poon-TAHNG SEHN-troh
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.meaningNote: "Pamasahe" refers to the fare for transportation such as a train, bus, or jeepney.
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.exampleSentence: Magkano po ang pamasahe papuntang kabayanan o sentro?

which-platform-for-the-airport.text: Saang platform po sasakay papuntang paliparan?
which-platform-for-the-airport.pronunciation: sah-AHNG PLAHT-fohrm poh sah-SAH-kye pah-poon-TAHNG pah-lee-PAH-rahn
which-platform-for-the-airport.meaningNote: "Paliparan" is the formal Filipino word for airport, though "airport" is also universally used.
which-platform-for-the-airport.exampleSentence: Saang platform po sasakay papuntang paliparan (airport)?

can-you-call-a-taxi.text: Puwede po ba ninyo akong tawagan ng taksi?
can-you-call-a-taxi.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bah neen-YOH ah-KOHNG tah-wah-GAHN nahng TAHK-see
can-you-call-a-taxi.meaningNote: Polite request asking a guard or receptionist to hail or book a taxi.
can-you-call-a-taxi.exampleSentence: Medyo maulan po, puwede po ba ninyo akong tawagan ng taksi?

do-you-have-wifi.text: May Wi-Fi po ba rito at ano po ang password?
do-you-have-wifi.pronunciation: my WAI-fai poh bah REE-toh aht ah-NOH poh ahng PAHS-wohrd
do-you-have-wifi.meaningNote: Everyday question at cafés, hotels, and guesthouses.
do-you-have-wifi.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang magtanong, may Wi-Fi po ba rito at ano ang password?

can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.text: Puwede ko po bang iwan muna ang aking bagahe nang ilang oras?
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.pronunciation: pweh-DEH koh poh bahng EE-wahn MOO-nah ahng AH-keeng bah-GAH-heh nahng EE-lahng OH-rahs
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.meaningNote: Polite request asking concierge or front desk staff to hold your bags temporarily.
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.exampleSentence: Mamayang gabi pa po ang biyahe ko, puwede ko po bang iwan muna ang bagahe ko rito?

do-you-accept-credit-cards.text: Tumatanggap po ba kayo ng card o cash lang?
do-you-accept-credit-cards.pronunciation: too-mahn-tahng-GAHP poh bah kah-YOH nahng kahrd oh kahsh lahng
do-you-accept-credit-cards.meaningNote: Checking whether cash is required or if cards and e-wallets are accepted.
do-you-accept-credit-cards.exampleSentence: Bago po ako bumili, tumatanggap po ba kayo ng card o cash lang po?

where-can-i-exchange-currency.text: Saan po puwedeng magpapalit ng pera nang ligtas?
where-can-i-exchange-currency.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh pweh-DEHNG mahg-pah-pah-LEET nahng PEH-rah nahng leeg-TAHS
where-can-i-exchange-currency.meaningNote: Looking for an authorized money changer or bank to exchange foreign currency.
where-can-i-exchange-currency.exampleSentence: May dalang dolyar po ako, saan po puwedeng magpapalit ng pera nang ligtas?

does-this-bus-stop-here.text: Humihinto po ba ang bus dito?
does-this-bus-stop-here.pronunciation: hoo-mee-heen-TOH poh bah ahng boos DEE-toh
does-this-bus-stop-here.meaningNote: In the Philippines, you can also ask "Dito po ba ang babaan o sakayan ng bus?".
does-this-bus-stop-here.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, humihinto po ba ang bus papuntang istasyon dito?

where-is-the-subway-entrance.text: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng tren o MRT?
where-is-the-subway-entrance.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng pee-nah-kah-mah-LAH-peet nah ees-tahs-YOHN nahng trehn oh ehm-ahr-TEE
where-is-the-subway-entrance.meaningNote: In Metro Manila, urban rail lines are referred to as the "LRT" or "MRT".
where-is-the-subway-entrance.exampleSentence: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng MRT mula rito?

where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.text: Saan po puwedeng bumili ng beep card o tiket?
where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh pweh-DEHNG boo-mee-LEE nahng beep kahrd oh TEE-keht
where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.meaningNote: "Beep card" is the reloadable stored-value transit card used on Philippine trains and select buses.
where-can-i-buy-a-transit-card.exampleSentence: Saan po puwedeng bumili ng beep card para sa tren?

how-much-is-the-fare.meaningNote: "Pamasahe" is the universal word for fare on buses, jeepneys, tricycles, and trains.
how-much-is-the-fare.exampleSentence: Kuya, magkano po ang pamasahe hanggang sa kanto?

which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.text: Aling bus po ang papuntang sentro ng bayan?
which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.pronunciation: ah-LEENG boos poh ahng pah-poon-TAHNG SEHN-troh nahng BAH-yahn
which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.meaningNote: In Philippine towns, the town center is also called "bayan" or "poblacion".
which-bus-goes-to-the-city-center.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, aling bus po ang papuntang sentro ng bayan?

does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.text: Papunta po ba sa airport ang tren na ito?
does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.pronunciation: pah-poon-TAH poh bah sah EHR-pohrt ahng trehn nah ee-TOH
does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.meaningNote: The English loanword "airport" (or formal "paliparan") is used in everyday speech.
does-this-train-go-to-the-airport.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, papunta po ba sa airport ang tren na ito?

what-time-does-the-next-train-arrive.text: Anong oras po darating ang susunod na tren?
what-time-does-the-next-train-arrive.pronunciation: ah-NOHNG OH-rahs poh dah-rah-TEENG ahng soo-soo-NOHD nah trehn
what-time-does-the-next-train-arrive.exampleSentence: Anong oras po darating ang susunod na tren?

where-should-i-get-off.meaningNote: "Bumaba" means to get off a vehicle. To ask a jeepney or bus driver to pull over right now, say "Para po!".
where-should-i-get-off.exampleSentence: Pupunta po ako sa museo, saan po ako dapat bumaba?

is-this-the-right-platform.text: Ito po ba ang tamang platform?
is-this-the-right-platform.pronunciation: ee-TOH poh bah ahng TAH-mahng PLAHT-fohrm
is-this-the-right-platform.meaningNote: The loanword "platform" is standard at Philippine train stations.
is-this-the-right-platform.exampleSentence: Ito po ba ang tamang platform papuntang hilaga?

please-take-me-to-this-address.text: Pakidala naman po ako sa address na ito.
please-take-me-to-this-address.pronunciation: pah-kee-dah-LAH nah-MAHN poh ah-KOH sah AH-drehs nah ee-TOH
please-take-me-to-this-address.meaningNote: You can also say "Pakihinto na lang po sa address na ito" when showing your destination to a taxi driver.
please-take-me-to-this-address.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, pakidala naman po ako sa address na ito.

where-is-the-check-in-counter.meaningNote: Airport terms such as "check-in counter", "boarding gate", and "boarding pass" are used in English across Philippine airports.
where-is-the-check-in-counter.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, saan po ang check-in counter para sa flight na ito?

where-is-the-departure-gate.meaningNote: In the Philippines, travelers and airport signs universally use "boarding gate" or "departure gate".
where-is-the-departure-gate.exampleSentence: Saan po ang boarding gate para sa flight papuntang Cebu?

where-is-immigration.meaningNote: The English term "immigration" is always used at Philippine international terminals.
where-is-immigration.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, saan po ang pila para sa immigration?

here-is-my-passport.meaningNote: Both "pasaporte" and "passport" are used in everyday conversation.
here-is-my-passport.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, heto po ang pasaporte at boarding pass ko.

i-am-here-for-tourism.meaningNote: "Para magbakasyon" (for a vacation/holiday) or "turista po ako" (I am a tourist) is the natural phrasing.
i-am-here-for-tourism.exampleSentence: Turista po ako; nandito po ako para magbakasyon nang dalawang linggo.

how-long-can-i-stay.text: Gaano po ako katagal puwedeng manatili rito?
how-long-can-i-stay.pronunciation: gah-AH-noh poh ah-KOH kah-tah-GAHL pweh-DEHNG mah-nah-TEE-lee REE-toh
how-long-can-i-stay.meaningNote: In casual speech, people also say "Hanggang kailan po ako puwedeng mag-stay?".
how-long-can-i-stay.exampleSentence: Gaano po ako katagal puwedeng manatili rito bilang turista?

i-have-nothing-to-declare.text: Wala po akong idedeklara sa customs.
i-have-nothing-to-declare.pronunciation: wah-LAH poh ah-KOHNG ee-deh-dehk-LAH-rah sah KAHS-tohms
i-have-nothing-to-declare.exampleSentence: Puro personal na gamit lang po ito; wala po akong idedeklara sa customs.

my-luggage-is-missing.meaningNote: Used at the airport baggage service desk when a checked suitcase does not arrive.
my-luggage-is-missing.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, hindi po lumabas sa carousel at nawawala po ang bagahe ko.

is-my-flight-delayed.text: Delayed po ba ang flight ko?
is-my-flight-delayed.pronunciation: dee-LEYD poh bah ahng flyt koh
is-my-flight-delayed.meaningNote: In Philippine airports, "delayed" and "flight" are universally used in everyday speech (formal Tagalog is "Naantala po ba ang biyahe?").
is-my-flight-delayed.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, delayed po ba ang flight ko o on time po?

could-i-have-a-window-seat.text: Puwede po bang sa tabi ng bintana ang upuan ko?
could-i-have-a-window-seat.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng sah tah-BEE nahng been-TAH-nah ahng oo-POO-ahn koh
could-i-have-a-window-seat.meaningNote: Saying "window seat po sana" is also universally understood at airline counters.
could-i-have-a-window-seat.exampleSentence: Kung may bakante pa po, puwede po bang sa tabi ng bintana ang upuan ko?

can-i-check-in-early.meaningNote: Philippine hotels universally use the English terms "early check-in", "check-in", and "check-out".
can-i-check-in-early.exampleSentence: Maaga po kaming dumating, puwede po bang mag-early check-in?

i-would-like-to-book-a-room.text: Gusto ko po sanang magpa-reserve ng kuwarto.
i-would-like-to-book-a-room.pronunciation: goos-TOH koh poh SAH-nahng mahg-pah-ree-SEHRB nahng KWAHR-toh
i-would-like-to-book-a-room.meaningNote: "Kuwarto" (or "room") is the standard word for a hotel room, and "sana" makes the request polite.
i-would-like-to-book-a-room.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, gusto ko po sanang magpa-reserve ng kuwarto para sa dalawang gabi.

do-you-have-any-available-rooms.text: May bakanteng kuwarto pa po ba kayo?
do-you-have-any-available-rooms.pronunciation: my bah-KAHN-tehng KWAHR-toh pah poh bah kah-YOH
do-you-have-any-available-rooms.exampleSentence: Magandang gabi po, may bakanteng kuwarto pa po ba kayo ngayong gabi?

i-would-like-to-check-in.text: Magche-check in na po sana ako.
i-would-like-to-check-in.pronunciation: mahg-cheh-CHEHK een nah poh SAH-nah ah-KOH
i-would-like-to-check-in.meaningNote: Natural conversational phrasing at a Philippine hotel reception desk.
i-would-like-to-check-in.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, magche-check in na po sana ako.

i-would-like-to-check-out.meaningNote: Use "ako" for "I" (solo traveler) or "kami" for "we" (a group).
i-would-like-to-check-out.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, aalis na po kami at magche-check out na po.

what-time-is-breakfast-served.exampleSentence: Anong oras po ang almusal bukas ng umaga?

is-breakfast-included.text: Kasama na po ba ang almusal?
is-breakfast-included.pronunciation: kah-SAH-mah nah poh bah ahng ahl-moo-SAHL
is-breakfast-included.exampleSentence: Kasama na po ba ang almusal sa bayad sa kuwarto?

how-do-i-use-the-air-conditioning.meaningNote: In the Philippines, air conditioning is universally called "aircon", and "buksan" is used for turning on appliances.
how-do-i-use-the-air-conditioning.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, paano po buksan ang aircon sa kuwarto?

could-i-have-an-extra-towel.text: Puwede po bang makahingi ng dagdag na tuwalya?
could-i-have-an-extra-towel.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mah-kah-HEENG-ee nahng dahg-DAHG nah too-WAHL-yah
could-i-have-an-extra-towel.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang makahingi ng dagdag na tuwalya sa room 302?

there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.text: May problema po sa kuwarto ko.
there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.pronunciation: my proh-BLEH-mah poh sah KWAHR-toh koh
there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.meaningNote: Polite way to let reception know something in the room needs maintenance.
there-is-a-problem-with-my-room.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, may problema po sa kuwarto ko; mahina po ang tubig.

is-there-toilet-paper.text: Paumanhin po, wala na pong tissue sa CR.
is-there-toilet-paper.pronunciation: pow-mahn-HEEN poh, wah-LAH nah pohng TEE-shyoo sah see-AHR
is-there-toilet-paper.meaningNote: In the Philippines, toilet paper is almost always called "tissue", and the restroom is called "CR" (Comfort Room) or "banyo".
is-there-toilet-paper.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, wala na pong tissue sa CR.

is-there-a-baby-changing-table.text: May palitan po ba ng diaper ng baby rito?
is-there-a-baby-changing-table.pronunciation: my pah-lee-TAHN poh bah nahng DYE-pehr nahng BEY-bee REE-toh
is-there-a-baby-changing-table.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, may palitan po ba ng diaper ng baby rito sa banyo?

is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.text: May malapit po bang CR o banyo rito?
is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.pronunciation: my mah-LAH-peet poh bahng see-AHR oh BAHN-yoh REE-toh
is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.meaningNote: Everyone in the Philippines understands "CR" (Comfort Room) and "banyo".
is-there-a-public-restroom-nearby.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, may malapit po bang CR o banyo rito sa parke?

is-this-restroom-free.text: Libre po ba ang paggamit ng CR?
is-this-restroom-free.pronunciation: LEEB-reh poh bah ahng pahg-gah-MEET nahng see-AHR
is-this-restroom-free.meaningNote: Some public restrooms at terminals and markets charge 5 to 10 pesos.
is-this-restroom-free.exampleSentence: Libre po ba ang paggamit ng CR o may bayad po?

is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.text: Panlalaki po ba o pambabae ang CR na ito?
is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.pronunciation: pahn-lah-LAH-kee poh bah oh pahm-bah-BAH-eh ahng see-AHR nah ee-TOH
is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.meaningNote: "Panlalaki" means for men, and "pambabae" means for women.
is-this-restroom-for-men-or-women.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, panlalaki po ba o pambabae ang CR na ito?

may-i-use-your-restroom.text: Puwede po bang makigamit ng banyo ninyo?
may-i-use-your-restroom.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mah-kee-gah-MEET nahng BAHN-yoh neen-YOH
may-i-use-your-restroom.meaningNote: The prefix "maki-" ("makigamit") politely asks permission to share or use someone else's facility.
may-i-use-your-restroom.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, puwede po bang makigamit ng banyo ninyo?

is-there-a-wheelchair-accessible-restroo.text: May CR po ba rito para sa naka-wheelchair o PWD?
is-there-a-wheelchair-accessible-restroo.pronunciation: my see-AHR poh bah REE-toh PAH-rah sah nah-kah-WEEL-chehr oh pee-dah-bohl-yoo-DEE
is-there-a-wheelchair-accessible-restroo.meaningNote: In the Philippines, accessible facilities are commonly labeled "PWD" (Person with Disability).
is-there-a-wheelchair-accessible-restroo.exampleSentence: May CR po ba rito sa baba para sa naka-wheelchair o PWD?

where-can-i-wash-my-hands.text: Saan po puwedeng maghugas ng kamay?
where-can-i-wash-my-hands.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh pweh-DEHNG mahg-HOO-gahs nahng kah-MY
where-can-i-wash-my-hands.meaningNote: "Maghugas ng kamay" means to wash one's hands.
where-can-i-wash-my-hands.exampleSentence: Bago po kami kumain, saan po puwedeng maghugas ng kamay?

is-there-a-shower-available.text: May paliguan o shower po ba rito?
is-there-a-shower-available.pronunciation: my pah-lee-GOO-ahn oh SHAW-wehr poh bah REE-toh
is-there-a-shower-available.meaningNote: "Paliguan" or "banlawan" (rinse area at beaches) and "shower" are commonly used.
is-there-a-shower-available.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, may paliguan o shower po ba malapit sa beach?

where-is-a-drinking-fountain.text: Saan po may inuming tubig o water station?
where-is-a-drinking-fountain.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh my ee-noo-MEENG TOO-beeg oh WAH-tehr STEY-shohn
where-is-a-drinking-fountain.meaningNote: Looking for drinking water or a refill station.
where-is-a-drinking-fountain.exampleSentence: Saan po may inuming tubig para malagyan ang bote ko?

where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.text: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na pasyalan dito?
where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng pee-nah-kah-mah-LAH-peet nah pahs-YAH-lahn DEE-toh
where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.meaningNote: "Pasyalan" is the natural Filipino word for a place to visit, stroll, or sightsee.
where-is-the-nearest-tourist-attraction.exampleSentence: May libre po kaming oras, saan po ang pinakamalapit na pasyalan dito?

how-much-is-the-entrance-fee.meaningNote: "Entrance fee" (or "bayad sa pagpasok") is universally used at museums, parks, and beaches.
how-much-is-the-entrance-fee.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, magkano po ang entrance fee para sa matanda?

do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.text: Kailangan po bang magpa-reserve nang maaga?
do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN poh bahng mahg-pah-ree-SEHRB nahng mah-AH-gah
do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.meaningNote: Checking whether advance booking is required.
do-i-need-to-book-in-advance.exampleSentence: Kailangan po bang magpa-reserve nang maaga bago pumunta roon?

is-photography-allowed.text: Puwede po bang kumuha ng litrato rito?
is-photography-allowed.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng koo-MOO-hah nahng lee-TRAH-toh REE-toh
is-photography-allowed.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, puwede po bang kumuha ng litrato sa loob ng museo?

could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.text: Puwede po bang pakikuhanan kami ng picture?
could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng pah-kee-koo-HAH-nahn kah-MEE nahng PEEK-choor
could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.meaningNote: Saying "Pakikuhanan naman po kami ng picture" (or "litrato") is the most natural way to ask someone to take your photo.
could-you-take-a-photo-of-us.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, puwede po bang pakikuhanan kami ng picture dito?

is-there-a-guided-tour.text: May guided tour po ba rito?
is-there-a-guided-tour.pronunciation: my GYE-dehd toor poh bah REE-toh
is-there-a-guided-tour.meaningNote: You can also ask "May tour guide po ba na puwedeng kunin?".
is-there-a-guided-tour.exampleSentence: May guided tour po ba rito ngayong hapon?

where-is-the-ticket-office.text: Saan po ang bilihan ng tiket?
where-is-the-ticket-office.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng bee-lee-HAHN nahng TEE-keht
where-is-the-ticket-office.meaningNote: "Bilihan ng tiket" literally means ticket buying booth/counter.
where-is-the-ticket-office.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, saan po ang bilihan ng tiket para sa tour?

is-this-place-open-today.text: Bukas po ba ang lugar na ito ngayon?
is-this-place-open-today.pronunciation: boo-KAHS poh bah ahng loo-GAHR nah ee-TOH ngah-YOHN
is-this-place-open-today.meaningNote: Note that "bukás" (stressed on the second syllable) means open, while "búkas" (stressed on the first syllable) means tomorrow.
is-this-place-open-today.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, bukas po ba ang lugar na ito ngayon?

how-long-does-the-tour-take.meaningNote: Asks how long the tour lasts from start to finish.
how-long-does-the-tour-take.exampleSentence: Gaano po katagal ang buong tour sa isla?

can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.text: May maire-recommend po ba kayong magandang pasyalan?
can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.pronunciation: my mah-ee-reh-reh-koh-MEHND poh bah kah-YOHNG mah-gahn-DAHNG pahs-YAH-lahn
can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.meaningNote: You can also use the Spanish-derived form "mairekomenda".
can-you-recommend-a-place-to-visit.exampleSentence: Bago lang po kami rito, may maire-recommend po ba kayong magandang pasyalan?

where-is-the-nearest-atm.text: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na ATM?
where-is-the-nearest-atm.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng pee-nah-kah-mah-LAH-peet nah ey-tee-EHM
where-is-the-nearest-atm.meaningNote: "ATM" is universally used across the Philippines.
where-is-the-nearest-atm.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, saan po ang pinakamalapit na ATM dito sa mall?

do-you-have-change-for-this.text: May panukli po ba kayo sa buong pera?
do-you-have-change-for-this.pronunciation: my pah-nook-LEE poh bah kah-YOH sah boo-OHNG PEH-rah
do-you-have-change-for-this.meaningNote: "Panukli" (from "sukli", change) means change for a large bill ("buong pera"), and "barya" means coins or small bills.
do-you-have-change-for-this.exampleSentence: Buo po ang pera ko, may panukli po ba kayo rito?

what-is-the-exchange-rate.text: Magkano po ang palitan ng dolyar ngayon?
what-is-the-exchange-rate.pronunciation: mahg-KAH-noh poh ahng pah-lee-TAHN nahng dohl-YAHR ngah-YOHN
what-is-the-exchange-rate.meaningNote: "Palitan" is the everyday word for the currency exchange rate.
what-is-the-exchange-rate.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, magkano po ang palitan ng dolyar ngayon?

can-we-split-the-bill.text: Puwede po bang hiwalay ang bayad namin?
can-we-split-the-bill.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng hee-wah-LYE ahng BAH-yahd NAH-meen
can-we-split-the-bill.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, puwede po bang hiwalay ang bayad namin?

my-card-is-not-working.text: Hindi po gumagana ang card ko.
my-card-is-not-working.pronunciation: heen-DEE poh goo-mah-GAH-nah ahng kahrd koh
my-card-is-not-working.meaningNote: Used when a payment terminal fails to read your card.
my-card-is-not-working.exampleSentence: Hindi po gumagana ang card ko sa terminal; susubukan ko po ang isa pa.

do-you-accept-cash.text: Tumatanggap po ba kayo ng cash?
do-you-accept-cash.pronunciation: too-mah-tahng-GAHP poh bah kah-YOH nahng kahsh
do-you-accept-cash.meaningNote: The English loanword "cash" is standard in Filipino.
do-you-accept-cash.exampleSentence: Tumatanggap po ba kayo ng cash dito sa counter?

can-i-pay-with-my-phone.text: Puwede po bang magbayad gamit ang telepono o QR?
can-i-pay-with-my-phone.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mahg-BAH-yahd GAH-meet ahng teh-LEH-poh-noh oh kyoo-AHR
can-i-pay-with-my-phone.meaningNote: In the Philippines, mobile QR payments (such as GCash or Maya) are very common.
can-i-pay-with-my-phone.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang magbayad gamit ang telepono o QR dito?

could-i-have-a-receipt.text: Puwede po bang makahingi ng resibo?
could-i-have-a-receipt.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mah-kah-HEENG-ee nahng reh-SEE-boh
could-i-have-a-receipt.exampleSentence: Salamat po, puwede po bang makahingi ng resibo?

i-think-i-was-charged-twice.text: Parang nadoble po yata ang singil sa akin.
i-think-i-was-charged-twice.pronunciation: PAH-rahng nah-DOHB-leh poh YAH-tah ahng see-NGEEL sah AH-keen
i-think-i-was-charged-twice.meaningNote: Adding "parang ... yata" makes pointing out a billing mistake very polite and non-confrontational in Filipino culture.
i-think-i-was-charged-twice.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, puwede po bang pa-check? Parang nadoble po yata ang singil sa akin.

is-there-an-additional-fee.text: May dagdag na bayad po ba ito?
is-there-an-additional-fee.pronunciation: my dahg-DAHG nah BAH-yahd poh bah ee-TOH
is-there-an-additional-fee.meaningNote: "Dagdag na bayad" (or "extra charge") means additional fee.
is-there-an-additional-fee.exampleSentence: Bago po namin ituloy, may dagdag na bayad po ba ito?

what-is-the-weather-like.meaningNote: "Panahon" means weather (as well as time or season).
what-is-the-weather-like.exampleSentence: Nakalabas na po ba kayo? Kumusta po ang panahon ngayon?

is-it-going-to-rain.meaningNote: "Uulan" is the future tense of "ulan" (rain), and "kaya" adds "do you think?".
is-it-going-to-rain.exampleSentence: Makulimlim po ang langit, uulan po kaya ngayong hapon?

it-is-very-hot-today.meaningNote: In casual speech, "Ang init po ngayon!" is also very common.
it-is-very-hot-today.exampleSentence: Napakainit po ngayong araw, sumilong muna tayo.

is-there-a-storm-coming.meaningNote: "Bagyo" refers to a typhoon or tropical storm.
is-there-a-storm-coming.exampleSentence: Malakas po ang hangin, may paparating po bang bagyo?

should-i-bring-an-umbrella.text: Dapat po ba akong magdala ng payong?
should-i-bring-an-umbrella.pronunciation: DAH-paht poh bah ah-KOHNG mahg-dah-LAH nahng PAH-yohng
should-i-bring-an-umbrella.meaningNote: "Payong" is used for both rain umbrellas and sun parasols.
should-i-bring-an-umbrella.exampleSentence: Maglalakad po kami mamaya, dapat po ba akong magdala ng payong?

what-is-the-weather-forecast.text: Ano po ang lagay ng panahon bukas?
what-is-the-weather-forecast.pronunciation: ah-NOH poh ahng lah-GYE nahng pah-nah-HOHN BOO-kahs
what-is-the-weather-forecast.meaningNote: "Lagay ng panahon" is the standard phrase for the weather forecast or weather condition.
what-is-the-weather-forecast.exampleSentence: Aalis po kami nang maaga, ano po ang lagay ng panahon bukas?

it-is-very-cold-today.meaningNote: In casual speech, "Ang lamig po ngayon!" is also very common.
it-is-very-cold-today.exampleSentence: Napakalamig po ngayong araw dito sa bundok.

is-the-air-quality-okay.text: Maayos po ba ang kalidad ng hangin ngayon?
is-the-air-quality-okay.pronunciation: mah-AH-yohs poh bah ahng kah-lee-DAHD nahng HAH-ngeen ngah-YOHN
is-the-air-quality-okay.exampleSentence: Maayos po ba ang kalidad ng hangin ngayon sa labas?

is-it-going-to-be-sunny-tomorrow.exampleSentence: Pupunta po kami sa dagat, maaraw po kaya bukas?

do-i-need-a-jacket.text: Kailangan ko po bang magdala ng jacket?
do-i-need-a-jacket.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN koh poh bahng mahg-dah-LAH nahng JAH-keht
do-i-need-a-jacket.meaningNote: The loanword "jacket" is standard in Filipino.
do-i-need-a-jacket.exampleSentence: Malamig po ba sa gabi roon, kailangan ko po bang magdala ng jacket?

help-me-please.text: Saklolo po! / Tulungan po ninyo ako!
help-me-please.pronunciation: sahk-LOH-loh poh / too-LOO-ngahn poh neen-YOH ah-KOH
help-me-please.meaningNote: "Saklolo" is the traditional urgent cry for help during an emergency.
help-me-please.exampleSentence: Saklolo po! Tulungan po ninyo ako, may magnanakaw!

call-an-ambulance.text: Tumawag po kayo ng ambulansya agad!
call-an-ambulance.pronunciation: too-MAH-wahg poh kah-YOH nahng ahm-boo-LAHN-syah AH-gahd
call-an-ambulance.meaningNote: Urgent request to bystanders during a serious accident or medical emergency.
call-an-ambulance.exampleSentence: May nawalan ng malay, tumawag po kayo ng ambulansya agad!

call-the-police.text: Tumawag po kayo ng pulis ngayon din!
call-the-police.pronunciation: too-MAH-wahg poh kah-YOH nahng poo-LEES ngah-YOHN deen
call-the-police.meaningNote: Calling for police assistance during a crime or dangerous situation.
call-the-police.exampleSentence: May nanggugulo po sa labas, tumawag po kayo ng pulis ngayon din!

where-is-the-nearest-hospital.text: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na ospital o klinika?
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng pee-nah-kah-mah-LAH-peet nah ohs-pee-TAHL oh KLEE-nee-kah
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.meaningNote: Asking for the location of the closest hospital.
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.exampleSentence: Masama po ang pakiramdam ko, saan po ang pinakamalapit na ospital?

i-need-a-doctor.text: Kailangan ko po ng doktor ngayon din
i-need-a-doctor.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN koh poh nahng dohk-TOHR ngah-YOHN deen
i-need-a-doctor.meaningNote: Requesting a medical doctor for an examination.
i-need-a-doctor.exampleSentence: Mataas po ang lagnat ng kasama ko, kailangan ko po ng doktor ngayon din.

where-is-a-pharmacy.text: Saan po may bukas na botika o parmasya?
where-is-a-pharmacy.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh my BOO-kahs nah boh-TEE-kah oh pahr-MAHS-yah
where-is-a-pharmacy.meaningNote: Pharmacies are commonly called "botika" or "drugstore" in the Philippines.
where-is-a-pharmacy.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko po ng gamot sa ubo, saan po may bukas na botika rito?

i-lost-my-passport.text: Nawala po ang aking pasaporte at pitaka
i-lost-my-passport.pronunciation: nah-wah-LAH poh ahng AH-keeng pah-sah-POHR-teh aht pee-TAH-kah
i-lost-my-passport.meaningNote: Should be reported immediately to the local police and your embassy.
i-lost-my-passport.exampleSentence: Naiwan ko po sa taksi kanina, nawala po ang aking pasaporte at pitaka.

i-cannot-breathe.meaningNote: Critical medical emergency requiring immediate air and medical attention.
i-cannot-breathe.exampleSentence: Pakiusap, bigyan ninyo ako ng espasyo, nahihirapan po akong huminga.

there-is-a-fire.text: May sunog po, lumikas na tayo sa gusali!
there-is-a-fire.pronunciation: my SOO-nohg poh, loo-MEE-kahs nah TAH-yoh sah goo-SAH-lee
there-is-a-fire.meaningNote: Urgent warning to evacuate immediately toward the fire exit.
there-is-a-fire.exampleSentence: May makapal na usok sa kusina, may sunog po, lumikas na tayo!

where-is-the-nearest-police-station.text: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng pulis?
where-is-the-nearest-police-station.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng pee-nah-kah-mah-LAH-peet nah ees-tahs-YOHN nahng poo-LEES
where-is-the-nearest-police-station.meaningNote: You can also say "police station" or "presinto".
where-is-the-nearest-police-station.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, saan po ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng pulis?

what-is-the-emergency-number.text: Ano po ang emergency hotline o numero rito?
what-is-the-emergency-number.pronunciation: ah-NOH poh ahng ee-MEHR-jehn-see HAHT-lyn oh NOO-meh-roh REE-toh
what-is-the-emergency-number.meaningNote: Direct question asking for the local emergency phone number.
what-is-the-emergency-number.exampleSentence: Pakisabi po, ano po ang emergency hotline o numero rito?

please-leave-me-alone.text: Pakiusap po, pabayaan na ninyo ako.
please-leave-me-alone.pronunciation: pah-kee-OO-sahp poh, pah-bah-YAH-ahn nah neen-YOH ah-KOH
please-leave-me-alone.meaningNote: Firm statement asking someone to leave you alone ("Layuan po ninyo ako" means "Stay away from me").
please-leave-me-alone.exampleSentence: Pakiusap po, pabayaan na ninyo ako ngayon.

someone-stole-my-belongings.text: May nagnakaw po ng mga gamit ko.
someone-stole-my-belongings.pronunciation: my nahg-NAH-kaw poh nahng mah-NGAH GAH-meet koh
someone-stole-my-belongings.meaningNote: Literal statement reporting theft of personal belongings.
someone-stole-my-belongings.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko po ng tulong; may nagnakaw po ng mga gamit ko.

i-need-a-police-report.text: Kailangan ko po ng kopya ng police report.
i-need-a-police-report.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN koh poh nahng KOHP-yah nahng poh-LEES ree-POHRT
i-need-a-police-report.meaningNote: In the Philippines, "police report" (or "blotter") is the standard official term.
i-need-a-police-report.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko po ng kopya ng police report, pakiusap.

my-wallet-was-stolen.exampleSentence: Ninakaw po ang pitaka ko habang nakasakay sa bus.

i-have-been-robbed.meaningNote: Direct statement reporting that you were robbed.
i-have-been-robbed.exampleSentence: Tulungan po ninyo ako, ninakawan po ako ngayon lang.

i-do-not-feel-safe-here.text: Hindi po ako panatag o ligtas dito.
i-do-not-feel-safe-here.pronunciation: heen-DEE poh ah-KOH pah-NAH-tahg oh leeg-TAHS DEE-toh
i-do-not-feel-safe-here.meaningNote: "Ligtas" means safe, and "panatag" means feeling secure.
i-do-not-feel-safe-here.exampleSentence: Hindi po ako panatag o ligtas dito; pumasok na po tayo sa loob.

i-need-to-report-an-incident.text: Kailangan ko pong mag-report ng insidente.
i-need-to-report-an-incident.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN koh pohng mahg-ree-POHRT nahng een-see-DEHN-teh
i-need-to-report-an-incident.meaningNote: Used at a police desk or barangay hall ("magpa-blotter" is also commonly used).
i-need-to-report-an-incident.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, kailangan ko pong mag-report ng insidente.

help-me-contact-the-embassy.text: Puwede po ba ninyo akong tulungang tumawag sa embassy ko?
help-me-contact-the-embassy.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bah neen-YOH ah-KOHNG too-LOO-ngahng too-MAH-wahg sah EHM-bah-see koh
help-me-contact-the-embassy.exampleSentence: Nawala po ang dokumento ko, puwede po ba ninyo akong tulungang tumawag sa embassy ko?

do-i-need-a-prescription.text: Kailangan po ba ng reseta ng doktor para sa gamot na ito?
do-i-need-a-prescription.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN poh bah nahng reh-SEH-tah nahng dohk-TOHR PAH-rah sah gah-MOHT nah ee-TOH
do-i-need-a-prescription.meaningNote: "Reseta" means a medical prescription, and "gamot" means medicine.
do-i-need-a-prescription.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, kailangan po ba ng reseta ng doktor para sa gamot na ito?

how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.text: Gaano po kadalas dapat inumin ang gamot na ito?
how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.pronunciation: gah-AH-noh poh kah-dah-LAHS DAH-paht ee-noo-MEEN ahng gah-MOHT nah ee-TOH
how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.meaningNote: You can also ask "Tuwing ilang oras po iinumin ito?" (Every how many hours should this be taken?).
how-often-should-i-take-this-medicine.exampleSentence: Gaano po kadalas dapat inumin ang gamot na ito sa isang araw?

i-have-travel-insurance.text: May travel health insurance po ako.
i-have-travel-insurance.pronunciation: my TRAH-behl hehlth een-SHOO-rahns poh ah-KOH
i-have-travel-insurance.meaningNote: Hospitals in the Philippines use the English term "travel health insurance" or "health insurance".
i-have-travel-insurance.exampleSentence: Heto po ang card ko; may travel health insurance po ako.

i-do-not-feel-well.meaningNote: Natural way in Filipino to say "I don't feel well".
i-do-not-feel-well.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko po munang maupo; masama po ang pakiramdam ko.

i-have-a-headache.meaningNote: "Masakit" means painful or aching, and "ulo" means head.
i-have-a-headache.exampleSentence: Kanina pa pong umaga masakit po ang ulo ko.

i-have-a-fever.exampleSentence: Nilalamig po ako at may lagnat po ako.

i-have-stomach-pain.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko pong magpatingin sa doktor dahil masakit po ang tiyan ko.

i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.text: May allergy po ako sa gamot na ito.
i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.pronunciation: my AH-lehr-jee poh ah-KOH sah gah-MOHT nah ee-TOH
i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.meaningNote: Clear statement informing medical or pharmacy staff of a drug allergy.
i-am-allergic-to-this-medicine.exampleSentence: Pakitingnan po sa rekord; may allergy po ako sa gamot na ito.

do-you-have-pain-relievers.text: May gamot po ba kayo para sa sakit ng katawan o pain reliever?
do-you-have-pain-relievers.pronunciation: my gah-MOHT poh bah kah-YOH PAH-rah sah sah-KEET nahng kah-tah-WAHN oh peyn ree-LEE-behr
do-you-have-pain-relievers.meaningNote: Pharmacists in the Philippines immediately understand "pain reliever".
do-you-have-pain-relievers.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, may pain reliever po ba kayo rito sa botika?

i-need-medical-assistance.text: Kailangan ko po ng tulong medikal.
i-need-medical-assistance.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN koh poh nahng TOO-lohng meh-dee-KAHL
i-need-medical-assistance.exampleSentence: Pakiusap po, kailangan ko po ng tulong medikal ngayon din.

i-lost-my-bag.meaningNote: "Bag" is the standard word in Filipino for a handbag, backpack, or travel bag.
i-lost-my-bag.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, nawala po ang bag ko kani-kanina lang.

has-anyone-found-my-phone.text: May nakapulot o nakakita po ba ng cellphone ko?
has-anyone-found-my-phone.pronunciation: my nah-kah-POO-loht oh nah-kah-KEE-tah poh bah nahng SEHL-fohn koh
has-anyone-found-my-phone.meaningNote: In the Philippines, a mobile phone is most commonly called a "cellphone" or "phone".
has-anyone-found-my-phone.exampleSentence: Doon po ako nakaupo kanina, may nakapulot po ba ng cellphone ko?

where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.text: Saan po ang opisina ng lost and found?
where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng oh-pee-SEE-nah nahng lohst ehnd fownd
where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.meaningNote: Malls, airports, and transit stations in the Philippines label and call this office "Lost and Found".
where-is-the-lost-and-found-office.exampleSentence: Excuse me po, saan po ang opisina ng lost and found dito?

i-left-something-here.text: May naiwan po akong gamit dito.
i-left-something-here.pronunciation: my nah-EE-wahn poh ah-KOHNG GAH-meet DEE-toh
i-left-something-here.exampleSentence: Kumain po kami rito kanina at may naiwan po akong gamit dito.

i-cannot-find-my-belongings.text: Hindi ko po mahanap ang mga gamit ko.
i-cannot-find-my-belongings.pronunciation: heen-DEE koh poh mah-HAH-nahp ahng mah-NGAH GAH-meet koh
i-cannot-find-my-belongings.meaningNote: "Mga gamit ko" means my belongings or things.
i-cannot-find-my-belongings.exampleSentence: Tiningnan ko na po sa kuwarto pero hindi ko po mahanap ang mga gamit ko.

i-lost-my-keys.text: Nawala po ang mga susi ko.
i-lost-my-keys.pronunciation: nah-wah-LAH poh ahng mah-NGAH SOO-see koh
i-lost-my-keys.exampleSentence: Paumanhin po, nawala po ang mga susi ko.

i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.text: Naiwan ko po ang bag ko sa tren.
i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.pronunciation: nah-EE-wahn koh poh ahng bahg koh sah trehn
i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.meaningNote: Direct statement for reporting an item left aboard a train.
i-left-my-bag-on-the-train.exampleSentence: Kabababa ko lang po at naiwan ko po ang bag ko sa tren.

please-call-me-if-you-find-it.text: Pakitawagan po ako kapag nahanap ninyo.
please-call-me-if-you-find-it.pronunciation: pah-kee-tah-WAH-gahn poh ah-KOH kah-PAHG nah-HAH-nahp neen-YOH
please-call-me-if-you-find-it.exampleSentence: Heto po ang numero ko; pakitawagan po ako kapag nahanap ninyo.

can-i-describe-it-to-you.text: Puwede ko po bang ilarawan sa inyo?
can-i-describe-it-to-you.pronunciation: pweh-DEH koh poh bahng ee-lah-RAH-wahn sah een-YOH
can-i-describe-it-to-you.meaningNote: In casual speech, people also say "Puwede ko po bang i-describe sa inyo?".
can-i-describe-it-to-you.exampleSentence: Kulay itim po iyong backpack, puwede ko po bang ilarawan sa inyo?

can-i-fill-out-a-form.text: Puwede po ba akong magsulat sa form?
can-i-fill-out-a-form.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bah ah-KOHNG mahg-soo-LAHT sah fohrm
can-i-fill-out-a-form.meaningNote: In the Philippines, "mag-fill out ng form" is also commonly used.
can-i-fill-out-a-form.exampleSentence: Puwede po ba akong magsulat sa form para maiwan ang contact number ko?

i-feel-very-dizzy.meaningNote: Warning sign of possible fainting or dehydration.
i-feel-very-dizzy.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang makahingi ng upuan? Nahihilo po ako at nanghihina.
